rules.like_for_like: a twin's outputs are a subset of its GPU cell's, with the same connectivity and the same reset scope (before / on the clock); every twin's arrays equal its oracle's
rules.no_dense_tile_path: every ch08 number of the story is ch08's first version (flood_fill.OLD_PATH: no K2b or K4b, the hybrid K3); the default engine (the dense-tile path) is timed on the frame for reference only; the dense lists are checked empty on every checked run

timing_note: GPU *_ms: one CUDA event before the first launch and one after the last, kernel-only (the image is already on the GPU and stays there). ch07 and ch08 time their init on the clock; ch01-ch05 and the loops reset their buffers on the device off the clock. Every run: image restored, two 96 MB L2-flush reads, sync, ~1.5 ms sleep kernel queued. Blocks of interleaved rounds (order reversed on odd rounds), at least the minimum, enough to span min_timed_s; a block not at full clocks runs again. est_* = v4's estimate: median sampled call x calls, each sampled call timed alone; host_clock_est_ms is v4's clock on the same calls. e2e = pageable H2D + pipeline + D2H (perf_counter), context only. CPU *_ms: @njit, one core, after all GPU work, in 5 interleaved rounds over every cell (median over all calls; round_medians show drift; cpu_rounds the host load). The twins (cpu_bfs4, cpu_bfs8, cpu_fill8, cpu_label, cpu_label_pre) run their oracle's loop on buffers allocated once per image, no paint; their reset (visited 0, depth -1, label -1) is untimed before each call or inside the timed call, as their GPU side resets its own (cpu_meta.reset). oracle_* and cpu_fill_canonical are the oracles as called, fresh arrays on every call (allocations included): reference only. twin.x = CPU twin / GPU median (> 1: the GPU is faster).

story.what: one block, shared-memory ring, against the 4-conn CPU BFS (depth, reset before the clock): the CPU still wins the small blob
one block (spill) against the 4-conn CPU BFS
two blocks, global queue, against the 4-conn CPU BFS
diagonals (8-conn) against the 8-conn CPU BFS (depth): row 2
one launch per blob (estimate) against the CPU labels (reset before the clock)
two blobs per launch with tags (estimate) against the CPU labels
the GPU finds its own seeds against the CPU labels: row 3
the tile BFS against the 8-conn CPU BFS without depth (reset on the clock): row 2
the tile waves (first version) against the CPU labels (reset on the clock): row 3
the tile BFS on the small blob against the 8-conn CPU BFS without depth: row 1
the CPU on the 81 Mpx frame (labels only, its reset on the clock: the whole job)
per-frame medians over 240 frames, the tile waves' first version (no dense-tile path), against the CPU labels; budget 33 ms
